facts.statement: The genus Ceratosaurus was first described by Othniel Charles Marsh in 1884.
facts.quote: authority: Marsh, 1884

facts.statement: The type species Ceratosaurus nasicornis was described from a nearly complete skeleton found in Garden Park, Colorado, within the Morrison Formation.
facts.quote: The genus was first described in 1884 by American paleontologist Othniel Charles Marsh based on a nearly complete skeleton discovered in Garden Park, Colorado, in rocks belonging to the Morrison Formation.

facts.statement: Ceratosaurus lived during the Late Jurassic period, approximately 155 million years ago, in North America and Europe.
facts.quote: Ceratosaurus (from Greek / 'horn' and σαῦρος 'lizard') is a genus of carnivorous theropod dinosaur that lived during the Late Jurassic period (around 155 m.y.a) in North America and Europe.

facts.statement: Ceratosaurus had very short but functional forelimbs with four fingers, the first three of which had claws.
facts.quote: The forelimbs were very short, but remained fully functional. The hand had four fingers with claws on the first three.

facts.statement: Most paleontologists no longer accept C. dentisulcatus and C. magnicornis as valid species, suggesting the skeletons may represent different growth stages of C. nasicornis.
facts.quote: These species are no longer accepted by most paleontologists, and all three skeletons possibly represent different growth stages of the same species.

facts.statement: It is debated whether fragmentary remains from Tanzania, Uruguay, and Switzerland belong to Ceratosaurus, as most paleontologists do not currently accept this assignment.
facts.quote: Fragmentary remains have also been reported from Tanzania, Uruguay, and Switzerland, although their assignment to Ceratosaurus is currently not accepted by most paleontologists.

facts.statement: While some paleontologists suggested Ceratosaurus hunted aquatic prey like fish, recent studies reject this in favor of it preying on plant-eating dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Ceratosaurus may have preyed upon plant-eating dinosaurs; while some paleontologists suggested that it hunted aquatic prey such as fish, this has been rejected by more recent studies.

facts.statement: It is debated whether the nasal horn was a weapon as Marsh originally suggested, with modern views favoring its use for display only.
facts.quote: The nasal horn was probably not used as a weapon as was originally suggested by Marsh, but more likely was used solely for display.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen USNM 4735 was discovered and excavated by farmer Marshall Parker Felch in 1883 and 1884.
facts.quote: The first specimen, holotype USNM 4735, was discovered and excavated by farmer Marshall Parker Felch in 1883 and 1884.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen was found encased in hard sandstone, which caused significant distortion of the skull and spine during fossilization.
facts.quote: The specimen was found encased in hard sandstone, leading to the skull and spine being heavily distorted during fossilization.

facts.statement: Charles Gilmore published an extensive redescription of the Ceratosaurus holotype and other specimens from New Haven in 1920.
facts.quote: In 1920, Charles Gilmore published an extensive redescription of this and the other theropod specimens received from New Haven, including the nearly complete Allosaurus specimen recovered from the same quarry.

facts.statement: Between 2014 and 2019, the Ceratosaurus holotype was dismantled and freed from its encasing plaque during a museum renovation.
facts.quote: In the course of the renovation of the museum's dinosaur exhibition between 2014 and 2019, the specimen was dismantled and freed from the encasing plaque.

facts.statement: A significant Ceratosaurus skeleton was discovered in the early 1960s by James Madsen and his team in the Cleveland-Lloyd Dinosaur Quarry in Utah.
facts.quote: a significant Ceratosaurus find was not made until the early 1960s, when paleontologist James Madsen and his team unearthed a fragmentary, disarticulated skeleton including the skull (UMNH VP 5278) in the Cleveland-Lloyd Dinosaur Quarry in Utah.

facts.statement: An articulated Ceratosaurus specimen was discovered in 1976 by Thor Erikson near Fruita, Colorado.
facts.quote: A second, articulated specimen including the skull (MWC 1) was discovered in 1976 by Thor Erikson, the son of paleontologist Lance Erikson, near Fruita, Colorado.

facts.statement: A Ceratosaurus specimen was discovered in 1992 in the Agate Basin Quarry in Utah.
facts.quote: A further specimen (BYU 881-12893) was discovered in 1992 in the Agate Basin Quarry southeast of Moore, Utah.

facts.statement: A juvenile Ceratosaurus skeleton was discovered in 1996 near Bone Cabin Quarry in Wyoming.
facts.quote: In 1996, a Ceratosaurus skeleton belonging to a juvenile individual was discovered near Bone Cabin Quarry in Wyoming.

facts.statement: Fragmentary Ceratosaurus remains have been found in the Morrison Formation.
facts.quote: fragmentary Ceratosaurus remains have been reported from various localities from stratigraphic zones 2 and 4-6 of the Morrison Formation

facts.statement: In 1896, Othniel Charles Marsh used the name Labrosaurus sulcatus for a single tooth found in Como Bluff.
facts.quote: In 1896, Marsh used the name Labrosaurus sulcatus in a caption for a figure depicting a single tooth (YPM 1936).

facts.statement: German expeditions uncovered dinosaur remains in the Tendaguru Formation in Tanzania between 1909 and 1913.
facts.quote: From 1909 to 1913, German expeditions of the Berlin Museum für Naturkunde uncovered a diverse dinosaur fauna from the Tendaguru Formation in German East Africa, in what is now Tanzania.

facts.statement: In 1920, Werner Janensch assigned three juvenile dorsal vertebrae from the Tendaguru Formation to Ceratosaurus.
facts.quote: In 1920, German paleontologist Werner Janensch assigned three dorsal vertebrae of a juvenile individual from the quarry "TL" to Ceratosaurus, as Ceratosaurus sp. (of uncertain species).

facts.statement: In 1925, Werner Janensch named the species Ceratosaurus roechlingi based on fragmentary remains from the Tendaguru Formation.
facts.quote: In 1925, Janensch named a new species of Ceratosaurus, C. roechlingi, based on fragmentary remains from the quarry "Mw" encompassing a quadrate bone, a fibula, fragmentary caudal vertebrae, and other fragments.

facts.statement: In 2000 and 2006, Octávio Mateus and colleagues described a Ceratosaurus specimen from the Lourinhã Formation in Portugal.
facts.quote: In 2000 and 2006, paleontologists led by Octávio Mateus described a find from the Lourinhã Formation of central-west Portugal (ML 352) as a new specimen of Ceratosaurus

facts.statement: A single Ceratosaurus tooth was found in Moutier, Switzerland.
facts.quote: Other reports include a single tooth found in Moutier, Switzerland.

facts.statement: In 2008, Matías Soto and Daniel Perea described Ceratosaurus teeth from the Tacuarembó Formation in Uruguay.
facts.quote: In 2008, Matías Soto and Daniel Perea described teeth from the Tacuarembó Formation in Uruguay, including a presumed premaxillary tooth crown.

facts.statement: In 2000, Madsen and Welles described two new Ceratosaurus species, C. dentisulcatus and C. magnicornis, based on specimens from Utah and Colorado.
facts.quote: Both the Fruita and Cleveland-Lloyd specimens were described by Madsen and Samuel Paul Welles in a 2000 monograph, with the Utah specimen being assigned to the new species C. dentisulcatus and the Colorado specimen being assigned to the new species C. magnicornis.

facts.statement: As of 2025, the species C. dentisulcatus and C. magnicornis are generally considered synonyms of C. nasicornis.
facts.quote: As of 2025, both species are generally considered as synonyms of C. nasicornis.

facts.statement: Brooks Britt and colleagues suggested in 2000 that C. nasicornis is a juvenile and that C. dentisulcatus and C. magnicornis represent the adult form of a single species.
facts.quote: Brooks Britt and colleagues, in 2000, claimed that the C. nasicornis holotype was in fact a juvenile individual, with the two larger species representing the adult state of a single species.

facts.statement: Oliver Rauhut and Matthew Carrano with Scott Sampson suggested that differences between Ceratosaurus species represent age-related or individual variation.
facts.quote: Oliver Rauhut, in 2003, and Matthew Carrano and Scott Sampson, in 2008, considered the anatomical differences between these species to represent ontogenetic (age-related) or individual variation.

facts.statement: Some authors question whether the Tendaguru finds belong to Ceratosaurus because they lack diagnostic features of the genus.
facts.quote: Other authors questioned the assignment of any of the Tendaguru finds to Ceratosaurus, noting that none of these specimens displays features diagnostic for that genus.

facts.statement: In 2011, Oliver Rauhut classified C. roechlingi and L. (?) stechowi as doubtful names because they are not diagnostic at the genus level.
facts.quote: In 2011, Rauhut found both C. roechlingi and Labrosaurus (?) stechowi to be possible ceratosaurids, but found them to be undiagnostic at genus level and designated them as nomina dubia (doubtful names).

facts.statement: In 2015, Elisabete Malafaia and colleagues assigned a Portuguese specimen to Ceratosaurus aff. C. nasicornis after questioning the validity of C. dentisulcatus.
facts.quote: In 2015, Elisabete Malafaia and colleagues, who questioned the validity of C. dentisulcatus, assigned the specimen to Ceratosaurus aff. Ceratosaurus nasicornis.

facts.statement: Portuguese Ceratosaurus remains are from the late Kimmeridgian age.
facts.quote: The bones were found embedded in yellow to brown, fine-grained sandstones, which were deposited by rivers as floodplain deposits and belong to the lower levels of the Porto Novo Member, which is thought to be late Kimmeridgian in age.

facts.statement: The Cleveland-Lloyd specimen is one of the largest known Ceratosaurus specimens.
facts.quote: This find represents one of the largest-known Ceratosaurus specimens.

facts.statement: The Colorado Ceratosaurus skull was found disarticulated and strongly flattened sideways.
facts.quote: The skull, although reasonably complete, was found disarticulated and is strongly flattened sideways.

facts.statement: The Colorado Ceratosaurus specimen was large but had not reached adult size, indicated by unfused skull sutures.
facts.quote: Although it was a large individual, it had not yet reached adult size, as indicated by unfused sutures between the skull bones.

facts.statement: The name C. magnicornis refers to a larger nasal horn.
facts.quote: Magnicornis points to the larger nasal horn.

facts.statement: The Wyoming juvenile Ceratosaurus specimen is 34% smaller than the holotype and includes a complete skull and pelvis.
facts.quote: This specimen is 34% smaller than the C. nasicornis holotype and consists of a complete skull as well as 30% of the remainder of the skeleton including a complete pelvis.

facts.statement: The C. roechlingi specimen is substantially larger than the C. nasicornis holotype.
facts.quote: This specimen stems from an individual substantially larger than the C. nasicornis holotype.

facts.statement: The Colorado Ceratosaurus skull was found strongly flattened sideways.
facts.quote: The skull, although reasonably complete, was found disarticulated and is strongly flattened sideways.

facts.statement: Ceratosaurus was a bipedal dinosaur that moved on powerful legs with reduced arms.
facts.quote: As a biped, it moved on powerful legs, while its arms were reduced in size.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen USNM 4735 of Ceratosaurus nasicornis was estimated to be 5.3 m or 5.69 m long.
facts.quote: Specimen USNM 4735, the first discovered skeleton and holotype of Ceratosaurus nasicornis, was an individual 5.3 m or 5.69 m long according to separate sources.

facts.statement: The first discovered skeleton of Ceratosaurus nasicornis is specimen USNM 4735.
facts.quote: Specimen USNM 4735, the first discovered skeleton and holotype of Ceratosaurus nasicornis, was an individual 5.3 m or 5.69 m long according to separate sources.

facts.statement: Othniel Charles Marsh described Ceratosaurus in 1884.
facts.quote: Othniel Charles Marsh, in 1884, suggested that this specimen weighed about half as much as the contemporary Allosaurus.

facts.statement: Recent estimates for the weight of the holotype Ceratosaurus range from 418 kg to 670 kg.
facts.quote: In more recent accounts, this was revised to 418 kg, 524 kg, or 670 kg.

facts.statement: Specimen UMNH VP 5278 was initially estimated at 8.8 m long but later revised to 7 m long.
facts.quote: The first of these, UMNH VP 5278, was estimated by James Madsen to have been around 8.8 m long, but was later estimated at 7 m long.

facts.statement: In 2020, Foster estimated the weight of specimen MWC 1 at 438 kg.
facts.quote: The second skeleton, MWC 1, was estimated to be slightly larger than the holotype specimen by Foster in 2020, at 438 kg.

facts.statement: Specimen BYU 881-12893 was estimated to weigh 1120 kg by Sombathy and colleagues.
facts.quote: The third specimen, BYU 881-12893, was estimated at 1120 kg by Sombathy and colleagues.

facts.statement: Specimen ML 352 was discovered in Portugal in 2000.
facts.quote: Another specimen, ML 352, discovered in Portugal in 2000, was estimated at 6 m in length and 600 kg in weight.

facts.statement: Specimen ML 352 was estimated to be 6 m long and weigh 600 kg.
facts.quote: Another specimen, ML 352, discovered in Portugal in 2000, was estimated at 6 m in length and 600 kg in weight.

facts.statement: The skull of Ceratosaurus was quite large in proportion to its body.
facts.quote: The skull was quite large in proportion to the rest of its body.

facts.statement: The holotype skull of Ceratosaurus nasicornis measures 55 cm in length from the snout tip to the occipital condyle.
facts.quote: It measures 55 cm in length in the C. nasicornis holotype, measured from the tip of the snout to the occipital condyle, which connects to the first cervical vertebra.

facts.statement: The skull of specimen MWC 1 was estimated to be 60 cm long and 16 cm wide.
facts.quote: The fairly complete skull of specimen MWC 1 was estimated to have been 60 cm long and 16 cm wide.

facts.statement: The skull length of the largest Ceratosaurus specimen is estimated at 79 cm.
facts.quote: The skull length of the largest specimen is estimated at 79 cm in length.

facts.statement: The most distinctive feature of Ceratosaurus was a prominent horn on the skull midline behind the nostrils, formed from fused nasal bones.
facts.quote: The most distinctive feature was a prominent horn situated on the skull midline behind the bony nostrils, which was formed from fused protuberances of the left and right nasal bones.

facts.statement: The premaxillary bones at the snout tip of Ceratosaurus contained only three teeth on each side.
facts.quote: The premaxillary bones, which formed the tip of the snout, contained merely three teeth on each side, less than in most other theropods.

facts.statement: The holotype had 15 blade-like teeth on each side of the upper jaw.
facts.quote: The maxillary bones of the upper jaw were lined with 15 blade-like teeth on each side in the holotype.

facts.statement: In specimen UMNH VP 5278, the upper jaw teeth measured up to 9.3 cm in length.
facts.quote: In specimen UMNH VP 5278, they measured up to 9.3 cm long, which is equal to the minimum height of the lower jaw.

facts.statement: In the holotype, the upper jaw teeth were 7 cm long, surpassing the minimum height of the lower jaw.
facts.quote: In the holotype, they are 7 cm in length, which even surpasses the minimum height of the lower jaw.

facts.statement: The holotype had 15 teeth on each half of the dentary bone, though they are poorly preserved.
facts.quote: In the holotype, each half of the dentary, the tooth-bearing bone of the mandible, was equipped with 15 teeth, which are, however, poorly preserved.

facts.statement: The tail of Ceratosaurus consisted of approximately 50 caudal vertebrae and made up about half of the animal's total length.
facts.quote: The tail comprised around 50 caudal vertebrae and was about half of the animal's total length.

facts.statement: The tail of the Ceratosaurus holotype was estimated to be 9.33 feet long.
facts.quote: In the holotype, it was estimated at 9.33 ft.

facts.statement: In Ceratosaurus, the scapula was fused with the coracoid to form a single bone with no visible separation between the two elements.
facts.quote: The scapula (shoulder blade) was fused with the coracoid, forming a single bone without any visible demarcation between the two original elements.

facts.statement: Unlike most derived theropods that had three fingers, Ceratosaurus retained four digits on its hands, with the fourth digit being reduced in size.
facts.quote: In contrast to most more-derived theropods, which showed only three digits on each hand (digits I–III), Ceratosaurus retained four digits, with digit IV being reduced in size.

facts.statement: The foot of Ceratosaurus consisted of three weight-bearing digits, numbered II through IV.
facts.quote: The pes (foot) consisted of three weight-bearing digits, numbered II–IV.

facts.statement: Ceratosaurus is an extinct genus of three species of ceratosaurian theropod dinosaur.
facts.quote: Ceratosaurus (gr. "reptil con cuerno") es un género extinto con tres especies de dinosaurio terópodo ceratosáurido

facts.statement: Ceratosaurus lived during the late Jurassic Period, approximately 153 to 148 million years ago, in the Kimmeridgian and Tithonian stages.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Jurásico, hace aproximadamente 153 y 148 millones de años, en el Kimmeridgiense y el Titoniense

facts.statement: Fossils of Ceratosaurus have been found in what is now North America, Africa, Uruguay, and Europe.
facts.quote: en lo que hoy es Norteamérica, África, Uruguay y Europa.

facts.statement: The type species Ceratosaurus nasicornis is known mainly from five fragmentary skeletons including skulls found in the Morrison Formation in the western United States.
facts.quote: La especie tipo, Ceratosaurus nasicornis es conocida principalmente por cinco esqueletos fragmentarios incluidos los cráneos los cuales han sido hallados en la Formación Morrison, en el oeste de los Estados Unidos.

facts.statement: Ceratosaurus followed the typical body plan of large theropod dinosaurs, being bipedal and moving on powerful hind legs while its arms were reduced in size.
facts.quote: Ceratosaurus siguió el plan corporal típico de los grandes dinosaurios terópodos. Fue bípedo y se movió sobre poderosas patas traseras, mientras que sus brazos se redujeron en tamaño.

facts.statement: Ceratosaurus is characterized by having a horn-like structure on the dorsal part of its skull, located behind the nostrils.
facts.quote: Ceratosaurus se caracteriza por tener en su cráneo una estructura semejante a un cuerno en la parte dorsal de la cabeza, colocado atrás de las fosas nasales.

facts.statement: The tail of Ceratosaurus measured about half the total body length and was thin and flexible, featuring high neural spines along its mid-dorsal region.
facts.quote: Su cola medía alrededor de la mitad de la longitud total del cuerpo, y era delgada y flexible, con altas espinas vertebrales, que se presentaban en el medio de su dorso.

facts.statement: In the premaxilla, Ceratosaurus possessed three teeth with small mesial serrations.
facts.quote: En el premaxilar Ceratosaurus poseía tres dientes con pequeñas endentaduras mesiales.

facts.statement: In the pubis, Ceratosaurus had a large notch rounded below the obturator foramen.
facts.quote: En el pubis Ceratosaurus tenía una muesca grande, redondeada por debajo el agujero obturador.

facts.statement: Fossils assigned to the species Ceratosaurus nasicornis have also been found in the Lourinhã Formation in Portugal and possibly in the Tendaguru Formation in Tanzania.
facts.quote: También se han hallado fósiles asignados a la especie Ceratosaurus nasicornis, en la Formación Lourinhã en Portugal y posiblemente en la Formación Tendaguru en Tanzania.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Ceratosaurus corresponds to an individual approximately 5.3 meters long and 2 meters tall.
facts.quote: El espécimen holotipo de Ceratosaurus corresponde a un individuo de unos 5,3 metros de largo y 2 metros de alto

facts.statement: David B. Norman estimated in 1985 that the maximum length of Ceratosaurus was 6.1 meters.
facts.quote: David B. Norman en 1985 estimó que la longitud máxima de Ceratosaurus era de 6,1 metros de longitud

facts.statement: In 1884, Marsh suggested that Ceratosaurus weighed half as much as an Allosaurus, which he estimated at 2 tons.
facts.quote: Marsh en 1884, sugirió que Ceratosaurus pesaba la mitad de un Allosaurus, el cual estimaba que pesaba 2 toneladas.

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul estimated in 1988 that the holotype of C. nasicornis came from an animal weighing approximately 524 kilograms.

facts.statement: Two skeletons assigned to the new species C. magnicornis and C. dentisulcatus by James H. Madsen and Samuel P. Welles in 2000 were much larger than the holotype.
facts.quote: Dos esqueletos, asignados a las nuevas especies C. magnicornis y C. dentisulcatus por James H. Madsen y Samuel P. Welles en un trabajo de 2000, eran muchos más grandes que el holotipo.

facts.statement: The largest of these, C. dentisulcatus, was informally estimated by Madsen to be around 8.8 meters long.
facts.quote: El más grande de estos, C. dentisuclatus, fue estimado informalmente por Madsen en alrededor de 8,8 metros de largo.

facts.statement: Two species, Ceratosaurus roechlingi from Tanzania and Ceratosaurus meriani from Switzerland, are still considered dubious among the many species once named.
facts.quote: Dos especies, de las muchas que alguna vez se han nombrado, todavía son consideradas dudosas, Ceratosaurus roechlingi de Tanzania y Ceratosaurus meriani de Suiza
